# Implementation Plan: DTV CLI Commands — validate, report, expectation

## 1. Purpose

Add three missing command groups to the `development-toolchain-validator` CLI so the meta-optimization team can invoke DTV end-to-end from the command line:

- `validate <reference>` — trigger a validation run and display the report.
- `report {conflicts|drift|maturity|tool-baselines}` — surface cross-skill reports.
- `expectation {structural|cli} {list|create|get|delete}` — CRUD over expectation records.

All three groups follow the existing `reference` / `connection` patterns: subcommands built on `cli-core` that are thin HTTP wrappers around the DTV API.

## 2. Required Reading

```bash
prompt-manager skill read cli-steer api-steer utils-unification seam-discovery-and-enforcement
prompt-manager skill read scientific-debugging
prompt-manager skill read implementation-plan-authoring
```

Also review in-repo:

- `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/cli/domains/references/register.go` — canonical subcommand-group pattern (list/get/create/update/delete + `--json`).
- `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/cli/domains/connections/register.go` — filter/action pattern (`drift` action on a connection uses `POST`, plus `--reference`/`--skill` filters).
- `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/api/handlers/report.go` — report endpoints & response shapes.
- `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/api/handlers/expectation.go` — expectation CRUD endpoints.
- `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/api/domain/validation/model.go` — `ReferenceValidationReport` / `ConnectionValidationResult` shapes the `validate` command must render.

## 3. Problem Statement

The meta-optimization team depends on DTV for P2/P3 readiness checks, but the CLI currently exposes only `reference` and `connection` commands. Without `validate`, `report`, and `expectation` commands, the team has no scriptable way to:

1. Trigger validation of a reference and read the outcome.
2. Inspect cross-skill conflicts, content drift, maturity scores, or tool-baseline regressions.
3. Manage the structural and CLI expectations that drive validation.

Everything else in the DTV initiative (`dtv-meta-optimization-contract`) assumes these commands exist.

## 4. Scope

**In scope**
- CLI code under `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/cli/`.
- New domain packages: `cli/domains/validation`, `cli/domains/reports`, `cli/domains/expectations` (names TBD, see Contract Decisions).
- Registration in `cli/domains/domains.go`.
- CLI-level tests in `cli/cli_*_test.go` matching the existing struct-assertion style.

**Out of scope**
- UI changes.
- Database/migration work.
- API business logic changes (but see Risks §11 — the validation HTTP route may not exist yet).

**Acceptance allow:** `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/cli/**`

## 5. Current Technical Context

- CLI uses `github.com/vrooli/cli-core` via `cliapp.NewStandardScenarioApp` (`cli/app.go`).
- Subcommand groups are returned from `domains/domains.go::SubcommandGroups`.
- Each domain package exports a `Register(core *cliapp.ScenarioApp) cliapp.SubcommandGroup`.
- HTTP helpers live inline per package (`get`, `getWithQuery`, `request`) and call `core.Get` / `core.Request`.
- Output uses `cliapp.ListReport`, `cliapp.MutationReport`, `cliapp.OperationalReport` with a `--json` flag from `cliutil.JSONFlag(fs)`.
- `cliutil.ParseInterspersed` is always used instead of `fs.Parse` (so `validate my-ref --json` works).
- API endpoints already implemented (`api/handlers/report.go`, `api/handlers/expectation.go`):
  - `GET /api/v1/reports/conflicts` `[?reference_id=…&skill_id=…]`
  - `POST /api/v1/reports/drift` `{current_hashes: {…}}`
  - `GET /api/v1/reports/maturity`
  - `GET /api/v1/reports/tool-baselines`
  - `GET|POST|DELETE /api/v1/expectations/structural[/{id}]`
  - `GET|POST|DELETE /api/v1/expectations/cli[/{id}]`
- Validation API endpoints **are not yet implemented** — see §11 Risks. `api/main.go` wires only reference/skill/expectation/report handlers; no `validationHandler` exists.

## 6. Target End State

Running `development-toolchain-validator --help` lists three new subcommand groups:

```
reference       Manage references
connection      Manage skill connections
validate        Run validation against a reference
report          Inspect cross-skill reports
expectation     Manage structural and CLI expectations
```

Each new command:
- Parses args with `cliutil.ParseInterspersed`.
- Honors `--json` and `--api-base`.
- Renders human output by default, structured JSON with `--json`.
- Is exercised by at least one struct-shape test under `cli/`.
- Passes `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` inside `cli/`.

The `dtv-meta-optimization-contract` follow-up item can rewrite prompts to call these commands directly.

## 7. Implementation Strategy (Phased)

<!-- Phase ordering assumes D1/D2/D3 decisions are resolved before Phase 1 starts. -->

**Phase 0 — Resolve open decisions (workshop)**
- D1: How to handle the missing validation HTTP handler.
- D2: Report command shape (flag vs. subcommand).
- D3: Expectation command shape (nested vs. flat vs. type-flag).
- D4: Scope of `validate` (synchronous only, or include history/job).

**Phase 1 — `expectation` command group**
- No API-side work required; all endpoints exist.
- Create `cli/domains/expectations/register.go` with `Register(core)` returning a group.
- Subcommands: per D3 (default plan: `expectation structural list|create|get|delete` and `expectation cli list|create|get|delete`).
- Reuse the request/response shapes in `api/domain/expectation/model.go`.
- Add `cli/cli_expectation_test.go` mirroring `cli_reference_test.go`.

**Phase 2 — `report` command group**
- No API-side work required.
- Create `cli/domains/reports/register.go`.
- Subcommands: per D2. Each maps 1:1 to `/api/v1/reports/…` and renders a `cliapp.ListReport`.
- `drift` uses `POST` with a `--hash skill=hash,…` repeatable flag (matches `POST /api/v1/reports/drift` body).
- Add `cli/cli_report_test.go`.

**Phase 3 — `validate` command**
- Blocked on D1 (if we don't expand scope): verify the HTTP handler is registered in `api/main.go` and `POST /api/v1/references/{id}/validate` returns `ReferenceValidationReport`.
- If D1 says expand scope: add a handler in `api/handlers/validation.go` wired to the existing `domain/validation` services, then register in `api/main.go`.
- Implement `cli/domains/validation/register.go` with `validate <reference>` (accepts ID or slug, mirroring `reference get`).
- Output: `cliapp.OperationalReport` with summary (pass/fail/total), per-connection rows, and triage status when failures exist.
- Optionally add `validate history <reference>` per D4.
- Add `cli/cli_validate_test.go`.

**Phase 4 — Wire-up & smoke test**
- Register all three groups in `cli/domains/domains.go::SubcommandGroups`.
- Run `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` in `cli/`.
- Document new commands in `cli/README.md` if it exists; otherwise in `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/README.md`.

## 8. Contract Decisions

Pending workshop decisions — see `workshop/round-001.json`. Defaults below will be promoted to commitments once the user answers:

- **D1 — Validation API blocker:** recommended option is to *expand this item's scope to register the validation HTTP handler*, because the validation service/models already exist and only the handler+route is missing. Alternative is splitting a separate backlog item and blocking this one.
- **D2 — Report command shape:** recommended `report conflicts` / `report drift` / `report maturity` / `report tool-baselines` (subcommands), to match the existing `reference list` / `connection drift` pattern. Filter flags: `--reference <id>`, `--skill <id>`.
- **D3 — Expectation command shape:** recommended nested groups — `expectation structural …` and `expectation cli …` — matching the description and keeping the two resource types visibly distinct.
- **D4 — Validate command scope:** recommended synchronous `validate <reference>` only for v1. Add `validate history <reference>` once `GET /api/v1/references/{id}/validate/history` is confirmed live.
- **Output format:** human-readable by default, `--json` flips to `cliapp.PrintReportJSON`. No new formatters.
- **Dry-run support:** `expectation create` and `expectation delete` will forward `X-Dry-Run: true` when `--dry-run` is passed (matches `api/handlers/expectation.go:86`).

## 9. Testing Plan

Automated only — the feedback memory `feedback_testing_over_manual.md` says plans should use automated tests, not manual checklists.

**Unit-level (CLI structs)**
- `cli/cli_expectation_test.go`: assert request/response struct field parity with `api/domain/expectation/model.go`.
- `cli/cli_report_test.go`: assert each report response type parses and renders a non-empty `ListReport` for a fixture.
- `cli/cli_validate_test.go`: assert `ReferenceValidationReport` parses and renders a non-empty `OperationalReport`.

**Command-wiring**
- `cli/cli_core_test.go`-style assertions that each new command is registered, callable with `--help`, and returns a non-zero exit for missing required args.

**Build/integration**
- `(cd scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/cli && go build ./... && go test ./... -timeout 300s)` is the gate.
- `(cd scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/api && go test ./...)` must still pass if D1 expands scope.

**Scenario smoke (optional, post-implementation)**
- `vrooli scenario restart development-toolchain-validator` then run each command against a seeded reference.

## 10. Rollout / Validation Checklist

1. Workshop decisions resolved, plan promoted.
2. PR touches only files under `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/cli/**` (plus `api/**` if D1 = expand).
3. `go build ./...` passes in `cli/` and `api/`.
4. `go test ./...` passes in `cli/` and `api/`.
5. `vrooli scenario restart development-toolchain-validator` stays green.
6. `dtv-meta-optimization-contract` can reference the new command surface without scope slippage.

## 11. Risks + Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation HTTP handler is not registered (`api/main.go` has no validationHandler; `fix/dtv-validation-api` returns 404 in the backlog). Without it, `validate` has nothing to call. | High | Blocks Phase 3 | D1 picks the resolution path. Preferred: expand this item's scope to wire the handler (domain/validation already has models, checkers, and an executor). |
| CLI flags drift from API query param names (`reference_id` vs `--reference`). | Medium | Confusing UX | Mirror `connections/register.go` filter naming (`--reference`, `--skill`) exactly; keep query-key conversion in one helper. |
| Drift report body shape (`current_hashes`) is awkward from a shell. | Medium | Poor UX for the one command that uses `POST`. | Accept `--hash <skill_id>=<hash>` repeatable; build the map client-side. Document in help text. |
| Users pass slugs where IDs are required (or vice versa). | Medium | Errors mid-pipeline. | Reuse the ID-or-slug fallback pattern from `references/register.go:136`. |
| Output format divergence between `report`/`validate` and existing commands. | Low | Inconsistent UX. | Stick to `cliapp.ListReport` / `OperationalReport` — no bespoke renderers. |

## 12. Non-goals / Prohibited Patterns

- Do **not** implement business logic in the CLI; reports/validation stay in the API.
- Do **not** introduce a new output format or bespoke renderer — use `cliapp.*Report` types.
- Do **not** add retries, polling, or spinners; commands are synchronous one-shots.
- Do **not** widen acceptance to other scenarios or to the UI.
- Do **not** add pagination flags that aren't enforced by the API.
- Do **not** build a shared "client" package inside the CLI — inline helpers per existing domain packages.

## 13. Definition of Done

- [ ] All workshop decisions resolved and plan committed.
- [ ] `development-toolchain-validator validate <reference>` returns a real report (or is deferred with a clear tracking item per D1).
- [ ] `development-toolchain-validator report {conflicts|drift|maturity|tool-baselines}` works against a live API.
- [ ] `development-toolchain-validator expectation structural {list|create|get|delete}` works.
- [ ] `development-toolchain-validator expectation cli {list|create|get|delete}` works.
- [ ] Every new command supports `--json`.
- [ ] `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass in `cli/` (and `api/` if D1 expands scope).
- [ ] No files outside `acceptance_allow` are modified.
- [ ] `dtv-meta-optimization-contract` can be queued without CLI gaps.

  <skill id="swarm-manager-workshop-finalize" name="Swarm Manager Workshop Finalize"><![CDATA[
# Workshop: Finalize Plan Synthesis

## Purpose

Run the final synthesis pass for a non-research backlog item. Incorporate the latest answered workshop decisions into `plan.md`, reassess readiness against the updated plan, and write a finalize round that contains no new decisions.

This skill exists specifically to avoid the stale-plan gap after the user answers the final round. It is not a normal workshop round and must not generate fresh questions.

## Input Context

**Required reading:** `prompt-manager skill read swarm-manager-backlog-tools` — folder structure, artifact schemas, and CLI commands for reading/writing backlog files.

**Required reading:** `prompt-manager skill read implementation-plan-authoring` — canonical plan structure, mandatory sections, quality gates, and guardrails for `plan.md`.

**Required reading:** `prompt-manager skill read plan-skill-discovery` — use the existing required reading already embedded in the plan when synthesizing the final draft.

## Scope

**In scope:**
- Read the current `plan.md`, all prior workshop rounds, `spec.json`, optional research artifacts, and user files
- Incorporate the latest answered decisions into `plan.md`
- Re-score the 5 readiness dimensions based on the updated plan
- Write a finalize round (`workshop/round-NNN.json`) with zero decision items

**Out of scope:**
- Generating new decisions or proposals
- Asking clarifying questions
- Implementing the backlog item
- Writing `handoff/` artifacts directly — swarm-manager derives idea handoff packages later from the finalized backlog state when execution begins
- Modifying `archive/`

## Output Requirements

All writes via CLI using `--stdin` with a heredoc:
```bash
swarm-manager backlog file-upload --kind fix --name dtv-cli-validate-and-report --path <path> --stdin <<'EOF'
<content>
EOF
```

### This Pass Produces

1. **`plan.md`** — updated so it reflects the latest answered workshop decisions
2. **`workshop/round-002.json`** — finalize round with this shape:

```json
{
  "round": 002,
  "generated_at": "<ISO-8601 timestamp>",
  "mode": "finalize",
  "pending_synthesis": false,
  "readiness": {
    "problem_clarity": 0,
    "scope_defined": 0,
    "approach_solid": 0,
    "testable": 0,
    "risk_awareness": 0
  },
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "i1",
      "type": "info",
      "text": "Latest answered decisions were incorporated into the plan. Remaining gaps are ..."
    }
  ],
  "plan_updates": "Brief summary of what changed in the plan during finalization"
}
```

## Rules

- `items` must contain **only** `info` items. Zero decisions.
- Do not ask any new questions, even if gaps remain.
- If readiness is still below the threshold after synthesis, reflect that honestly in scores and info items so the user can choose to run another normal workshop round.
- Preserve the audit trail: write a new finalize round instead of mutating prior rounds.

## Instructions

You are running finalize round 002 for a swarm-manager backlog item.

**Item context:**
- Kind: fix
- Title: CLI Commands: validate, report, expectation
- Description: Add the missing CLI commands that the meta-optimization team needs to invoke DTV.

Commands to implement:
- development-toolchain-validator validate <reference> — Trigger validation run for a reference, display results
- development-toolchain-validator report --conflicts — Show cross-skill contradictions
- development-toolchain-validator report --drift — Show skills with content drift
- development-toolchain-validator report --maturity — Show skill maturity scores
- development-toolchain-validator report --tool-baselines — Show tool accuracy regressions
- development-toolchain-validator expectation structural list|create|get|delete — CRUD for structural expectations
- development-toolchain-validator expectation cli list|create|get|delete — CRUD for CLI assertions

All commands are thin wrappers over the API following the existing reference/connection command patterns. Depends on both validation API and report generation being complete.
- Priority: 2
- Tags: cli, commands, meta-optimization

### Processing Steps

1. Read the backlog item and all available artifacts:
   ```bash
   swarm-manager backlog get --kind fix --name dtv-cli-validate-and-report
   swarm-manager backlog files --kind fix --name dtv-cli-validate-and-report
   ```
   Then read:
   - `plan.md`
   - every file in `workshop/`
   - `spec.json`
   - `research/summary.md` if present
   - user-provided files
   - **Initiative context** — If this item belongs to initiative `dtv-meta-optimization-readiness`, check for strategic context:
     ```bash
     swarm-manager initiatives get --name dtv-meta-optimization-readiness
     swarm-manager initiatives files --name dtv-meta-optimization-readiness
     ```
     Read any files present (orchestration summaries, decision logs, strategy docs). Use initiative context to align decisions with the broader initiative goals and understand how this item relates to sibling items.

2. Find the latest answered workshop round.
   - Treat selected options, freeform text, and notes as authoritative user intent.
   - Incorporate those choices into `plan.md`.

3. Update `plan.md`.
   - Make the plan internally consistent with the latest answers.
   - Tighten sections that changed because of those answers.
   - Do not introduce placeholder questions or “TBD” sections unless the information is genuinely missing.

4. Re-score readiness against the updated plan using the normal 0-3 rubric.
   - Be honest.
   - If the plan is still not ready, note the remaining weak dimensions in info items.

5. Write `plan.md`.

6. Write `workshop/round-002.json`.
   - Set `"mode": "finalize"`.
   - Set `"pending_synthesis": false`.
   - Include only info items.
   - Summarize the synthesis outcome and any remaining gaps.

### Important

Do not create or update `handoff/` files during workshop finalization. The finalized `plan.md` and workshop state are the authoritative sources; swarm-manager regenerates the downstream idea handoff package from those files at process-time.
